module.purpose: Manages entanglement of concurrent async actions (transitions) in the React reconciler, providing a shared transition lane, a combined completion thenable, and optional isomorphic default transition indicators.
module.summary: This module implements the machinery for grouping multiple concurrent async actions into a single entangled scope so that React's concurrent rendering can treat them as one unit. It exposes functions to register an async action's thenable, peek at the shared lane or completion thenable, and manage default loading indicators that work across roots in an isomorphic way. Internal state tracks pending action count, listeners to notify on completion, and indicator lifecycle. It interacts with the scheduler, profiler timers, and feature flags but holds no classes.
module.businessContext: React concurrent transitions rely on this to suspend UI until all entangled async work finishes. Failure breaks loading states and transition batching.

units.name: chainThenableValue

detail.name: chainThenableValue
detail.signature: export function chainThenableValue<T>(thenable: Thenable<T>, result: T): Thenable<T>
preconditions: `thenable` must be a valid object implementing a `then` method accepting two optional callbacks.
`result` must be provided (not `undefined`-required by the type parameter).
The returned thenable is consumed exclusively by React's reconciliation layer; non-React consumers may observe pending state indefinitely.
postconditions: Returns a new thenable whose `.status` starts as `'pending'` until the upstream `thenable` settles.
When the upstream resolves, the returned thenable's `.status` becomes `'fulfilled'` and `.value` is set to `result` (not the upstream's resolved value).
When the upstream rejects, the returned thenable's `.status` becomes `'rejected'` and `.reason` is set to the upstream's rejection error.
Any listener registered via the returned thenable's `then` is invoked with `result` upon fulfillment, or with `undefined` upon rejection.
invariants: The returned thenable's `.status` only transitions from `'pending'` to `'fulfilled'` or `'pending'` to `'rejected'`; it never transitions once settled.
Listeners registered before settlement are invoked exactly once in registration order.
The override `result` is always the value delivered to listeners, decoupled from the upstream's resolved value.
edgeCases: If `thenable` is already settled (never possible per React usage, but defensively): listeners are queued lazily until `then` is called.
Listeners registered after the upstream has settled: they are invoked immediately with `result` or `undefined` (no deferred queueing).
The upstream rejects: `.reason` holds the error; listeners are still called using the fulfill-piggyback perf hack with `undefined`.
Multiple concurrent listeners registered before settlement: all receive `result` in FIFO registration order.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Behavior is undefined if `thenable` is not a thenable; React contract guarantees it always is.

stateMutations: Mutates the local `thenableWithOverride` object: sets `.status`, `.value`, and `.reason` upon settlement.
Does not mutate the input `thenable` or any external/global state.
detail.summary: Wraps a thenable so that when its upstream resolves, the override `result` value is propagated to all registered React listeners while mirroring the resolve/reject state onto the returned thenable.

specLiterals.role: Initial status of the returned thenable before upstream settlement.
Status set on the returned thenable when the upstream resolves.
Status set on the returned thenable when the upstream rejects.
